newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sends greenhouse taskforce overseas.
newsitem.headline: Australia sends greenhouse taskforce overseas.

text.p: The Australian government said on Sunday it will send a taskforce around the world in a final bid to sell Australia's opposition to greenhouse gas emission reduction targets ahead of the Kyoto climate summit in December.

Australia, a major coal exporter, is fighting European Union efforts to impose compulsory across the board targets, with Canberra instead arguing for goals tailored to suit individual countries -- a process known as differentiation.
The taskforce will visit Washington, Tokyo and London to explain Australia's views on climate change to senior government advisers, Prime Minister John Howard said in a statement.

"In the government's view, there is still time before the Kyoto meeting to develop a realistic and fair outcome based on differentiation that would have a better chance of being implemented than the options being proposed, in particular by the European Union," Howard said.
The European Union is pushing for parties to the United Nations Climate Change Convention to adopt targets to cut greenhouse emissions to 15 percent below 1990 levels by 2020.
Australia has privately raised the possibility of quitting the convention if unacceptable targets are imposed at a meeting of convention nations in Kyoto, Japan in December.
"Mandatory uniform targets for developed countries would be inequitable, in not sharing the burden of controlling greenhouse gas emissions fairly between countries," Howard said.
"They would be ineffective in failing to constrain the burgeoning emissions from the major developing economies," he said.
Japan has also indicated its opposition to blanket emission cuts and said the plan could cause serious problems at December's Kyoto talks.
